meta.title: Portolan: publish geospatial data as plain files
meta.description: Portolan publishes geospatial data as plain files in your own storage, with no servers, databases, or accounts. Cloud-optimized formats and structured metadata let people and agents work with and build on the data directly, while the registry links every catalog into a searchable network of open data.

hero.title: Publish geospatial data as plain files in your own storage,
hero.description: A catalog is a directory of open-format data on any S3-compatible bucket, described by structured <m>STAC</m> metadata, and it runs without servers, databases, or accounts. Cloud-optimized formats let people and agents query the data directly.

why.title: Spatial data infrastructure still assumes servers, databases, and specialists. Portolan doesn't.

open.title: Open and interoperable
open.description: Catalogs are built on established open formats like <m>GeoParquet</m>, <m>COG</m>, and <m>STAC</m> metadata, which work today in DuckDB, BigQuery, Pandas, QGIS, and ArcGIS. The standard and the tools are open source under <m>Apache-2.0</m>. If Portolan disappeared tomorrow, every file in a catalog would still work in the tools you already use.

peopleAndAgents.title: Ready for people and agents
peopleAndAgents.description: A catalog describes itself in plain text and structured metadata. A person can read what the data is and where it came from, and an agent can do the same, then query it with standard tools. The <link>Finland.SDI demo</link> shows an agent doing that across national datasets.

easy.title: Simple to operate
easy.description: Running spatial data infrastructure normally means GeoServer or an Esri stack, with databases, services, and staff to keep them up. A Portolan catalog has none of that. Building one still takes work, which is what the CLI and validator are for, but once published it needs no maintenance.

scalable.title: Scales with your storage
scalable.description: The same catalog works whether it holds megabytes or terabytes. With no servers to run, scaling is your cloud provider's problem, not yours.

lowCost.title: Low cost
lowCost.description: Your only costs are storage and egress, paid to your cloud provider. Sharing public data should not need an operations team, and a popular dataset should not blow a budget. The <link>cost calculator</link> shows what your data would run.

sovereign.title: Sovereign
sovereign.description: You choose where the data lives, including providers in your own country. Host on AWS, Azure, GCS, MinIO, Hetzner, Scaleway, or any S3-compatible storage. No one sits between your organization and its data.

howItWorks.title: From raw files to a published catalog.

convert.title: Convert
convert.description: Any input becomes cloud-native, legacy formats or new ones alike. Vectors turn into <m>GeoParquet</m>, rasters into <m>COG</m>, tiles into <m>PMTiles</m>.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.description: A <m>STAC</m> catalog describes every asset, so any <m>STAC</m> tool can read it.

publish.title: Publish
publish.description: Push the files to any S3-compatible storage, from AWS, GCS, and Azure to R2, MinIO, or Source Cooperative.

browse.title: Use
browse.description: Use it with standard geospatial tools like DuckDB, Sedona, and QGIS, or point an agent at the URL.

ecosystem.title: Each part raises the value of the others.

projects.spec: The standard. Defines what a great catalog looks like.
projects.rashid: The validator. Proves a catalog meets the standard.
projects.cli: The CLI. Makes catalogs easy to build.
projects.registry: The registry. Links every catalog into a searchable network.
projects.browser: The browser. Explore catalogs on the web.
projects.skills: Claude skills. Publish with an agent.

cli.title: With the CLI
cli.description: Install <m>portolan-cli</m>, then <m>init</m>, <m>add</m>, <m>check</m>, and <m>push</m>. The CLI converts your files and generates the catalog.

claude.title: With Claude
claude.description: Install the Portolan skill in Claude Code and point it at your data. It handles conversion, metadata, and publishing. Agents excel at CLIs and text files, so non-experts can publish too.

registry.title: Browse {count} catalogs
registry.description: A catalog of catalogs. Every entry names its producer, provider, and host, so you can tell an official catalog from a mirror and choose the source you trust.

cta.title: Have a catalog to share?
cta.description: Submitting a catalog opens a pull request against the registry repository.

submit.title: Submit a catalog
submit.successDescription: Your catalog will appear after review.
